subject: Accelerated invoice lane and credit safety-net
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@mediqhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediqhealth.com, Trevor Lang <trevor.lang@mediqhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Move to Net60 for Q4 ramp (PO attached)

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the onboarding help last month — traffic has ramped faster than we expected and the team wants to align billing with our supplier cadence. Attached is a PO for the upcoming month.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood move Mediq to Net60 for Q4 (Oct–Dec) while we stabilise cashflow?
- If Net60 isn’t possible, can you propose an interim schedule (e.g., Net45 + higher credit)?

We estimate monthly spend ~ $120k–160k during the pilot; we’d need a provisional credit line of $150k to avoid interrupting service.

I’ve attached the PO (Mediq_PO_20260910.pdf). Please let me know the fastest path — procurement is ready to sign any amendment.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
Head of Procurement
Mediq Health
Procurement | procurement@mediqhealth.com

---
Attachment: Mediq_PO_20260910.pdf (application/pdf, 142 KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@mediqhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Move to Net60 for Q4 ramp (PO attached)

Samantha —

Appreciate the PO and the heads-up on ramp. Short answer: we can support a temporary accommodation but we need to balance credit exposure and tax/VAT clarity. Proposed interim option below so you can share with finance:

Option A (preferred, faster):
- Net45 payment terms for the next 60 days.
- 25% upfront on the first two invoices of the ramp (applied to each invoice) to reduce initial exposure.
- Provisional credit cap: $100,000 for the first 30 days, review after two billing cycles.

Option B (conditional Net60):
- Net60 for Q4 with a $150,000 secured credit facility, subject to a standard credit check and receipt of two months of bank statements / financials.
- 1.5% monthly interest on overdue amounts beyond agreed terms (we prefer to avoid, but need deterrent).

For both options we need:
- Completed credit request form (I’ve attached the Redwood_credit_request_form.xlsx).
- Confirmation of VAT treatment and Mediq’s VAT registration number (to determine invoicing entity and reverse-charge responsibilities).

I’ve looped in Rishi (finance) and Laura (account executive) to expedite. If you can confirm which option Mediq prefers and upload the credit details, we’ll fast-track an amendment and provide a DocuSign link.

Warmly,

Logan Wright
Director, Account Management
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@mediqhealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Move to Net60 for Q4 ramp (PO attached)

Hi Samantha — looping in finance next steps.

Thanks for the PO. To move forward with Option B (Net60 + $150k credit) we’ll need the following to complete our underwriting:
- Completed credit request (attached) + signed PO.
- Last 2 quarters of unaudited financials OR accountant-prepared cashflow statement.
- Bank reference or trade reference contact.
- VAT number and confirmation if the reverse-charge mechanism applies (we'll issue invoices without VAT if Mediq self-accounting applies).

If gathering those documents will take >5 business days, we can provisionally implement Option A immediately: Net45 + 25% upfront for the first two invoices and a provisional $100k limit. Option A requires only the attached credit form and the PO.

One additional technical note on invoicing: if Mediq wants invoices sent to a shared finance inbox rather than procurement, please confirm the billing email (we recommend finance@mediqhealth.com). Also confirm whether you need separate invoices per legal entity (we can split by VAT entity).

If you’re okay, Logan and I can put the agreed terms into a short MSA amendment and send via DocuSign for signatures.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations (Finance)
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Logan / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We’ve reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to get the pilot through Q4 without interrupting service:

- Temporary terms: Net45 starting with October invoices.
- Upfront buffer: 25% on the first two invoices (applied as credit).
- Provisional credit cap: $100,000 for the first 30 days. Review metrics at the end of November to consider expanding to $150k and moving to Net60.
- Mediq will complete your credit form and provide last two quarters' P&L by next Wednesday (2026-09-22).
- VAT: Mediq confirms VAT reg # GB987654321; reverse-charge applies for UK invoices (please net VAT accordingly).

We’re good to sign an MSA amendment with these temporary terms — please send the DocuSign and we’ll have procurement sign today. I’m attaching the signed PO and a short note from treasury confirming their review.

Samantha Cole
Head of Procurement
Mediq Health
